keep: FORMAT: content/keep.json drives the Keep tab (src/app.html renderKeep, renderByHeart, renderKnow, renderFamily as 'At home', renderRule). Everything is draft. Pastoral parts (home customs, blessings) need a pastor's review, as for Family.

NEW LEARN TEXTS (content/memory.json): thirteen World English Bible passages extracted by script from the WEB (John 3:16; Matthew 22:37–40; Psalms 1:1–3, 46:1–3 and 10, 51:10–12, 90:1–2 and 12, 121, 130:1–6; Luke 1:46–55; Luke 2:29–32; Matthew 11:28–30; Philippians 2:5–11 and 4:6–7). PLEASE CHECK: the Apostles' and Nicene Creeds were typed from the 1928 (US) Book of Common Prayer, which is public domain; compare them line by line with justus.anglican.org/resources/bcp/1928/MP.htm and HC.htm. The 1662 BCP was avoided because of Crown copyright in the UK.

BY HEART, intro: 'Many monks knew all 150 psalms by heart' (the Rule of Benedict has the whole Psalter sung each week; monks learned it by heart); schoolchildren reciting Virgil and the catechism; preachers and statesmen quoting Scripture and Shakespeare. General claims; PLEASE CHECK the tone is not overstated.

ESSENTIALS: Ten Commandments in short form with the numbering note (Catholic/Lutheran; Jewish first word); Mark 12:29–31 and Matthew 7:12 (WEB); Hillel's saying (Shabbat 31a); the books of the Bible (Protestant 39 + 27; Catholic adds Tobit, Judith, 1–2 Maccabees, Wisdom, Sirach, Baruch and longer Esther and Daniel; Orthodox more); the twelve apostles from Matthew 10:2–4 WEB (Lebbaeus/Thaddaeus; Luke's 'Judas son of James'; Matthias, Acts 1:26); the Christian year (seasons, colours vary); cardinal virtues (Plato Republic IV; 'cardinal' from cardo, hinge; the name usually credited to Ambrose) and theological virtues (1 Cor 13:13); seven deadly sins (Evagrius's eight thoughts, Gregory the Great c. 590, Moralia XXXI); fruit of the Spirit (Galatians 5:22–23 WEB); works of mercy (Matthew 25:35–36; burying the dead from Tobit; spiritual works as traditionally listed); Westminster Shorter Catechism Q1 (1647), Heidelberg Q1 (1563, in our own words), Baltimore Catechism (1885) 'Why did God make you?'. PLEASE CHECK the Baltimore wording.

AT HOME, the year: PLEASE CHECK: the Advent wreath begun by Johann Hinrich Wichern at the Rauhes Haus, Hamburg, in 1839, on a cartwheel; Francis of Assisi's nativity at Greccio, 1223; Epiphany chalking C+M+B, Christus mansionem benedicat, Catholic and Lutheran custom in central Europe; Shrove Tuesday from 'shrive'; ashes and Genesis 3:19; Zechariah 9:9; 'Maundy' from mandatum (John 13:34); hot cross buns as a British Good Friday custom; the Easter greeting; Genesis 8:22. Harvest date is approximate (28 September used only to show 'coming up').

RULE OF LIFE: Exodus 20:8–11; Matthew 6:16; early Church fasting on Wednesdays and Fridays (Didache 8); Acts 4:34; Wesley's 'The Use of Money' (gain, save, give all you can); Ignatius of Loyola and the examen; Guigo II, The Ladder of Monks (12th century); the emperor Julian complaining that Christians cared for pagan poor too (Letter to Arsacius); pilgrimage to Jerusalem from the fourth century (Egeria). The fasting entry warns anyone with a health condition or a history of eating problems to fast from something other than food.
greats: LIVE LIKE THE GREATS (keep.json greats, tools/days/greats.py). PLEASE CHECK: Churchill's 1,200 lines of Macaulay (My Early Life, 1930); Lincoln to Hackett 1863 on Macbeth; Lincoln to Joshua Speed 1864 'profitably engaged in reading the Bible'; Possidius, Life of Augustine 22 (table verse) and 31 (penitential psalms on the wall); Bach's J.J. and S.D.G. and the Calov Bible note; Benedict Rule ch. 13 (Lord's Prayer aloud) and ch. 48 (idleness); Marcus Aurelius Meditations I.7 (Epictetus from Rusticus); Bonhoeffer's half-hour meditation (Life Together) and Gerhardt hymns in prison letters; Mandela's garden and morning exercise (Long Walk to Freedom), Invictus on Robben Island. Texts: Macaulay checked against Gutenberg #847; Macbeth V.5 against Gutenberg #1533; Gettysburg (Bliss copy), Invictus and Alexander's 'O sacred Head' typed from known public-domain texts: PLEASE CHECK verbatim. Invictus is framed honestly as a poem of courage, not faith.

GREATS, revised so every piece is one the sources tie to the person. PLEASE CHECK: Benedict's Rule ch. 9 (Psalm 95 at Vigils), ch. 12 (Psalm 51 at Lauds), ch. 13 (Lord's Prayer aloud), ch. 18 (Psalm 70:1 opening each hour; Psalm 91 at Compline); Marcus Aurelius, Meditations X.34 quoting Iliad VI.146ff; Augustine, Confessions VIII.12 (Romans 13:13-14) and IX.4 (Psalm 4); Lincoln's House Divided speech (16 June 1858) and Psalm 19:9 in the Second Inaugural; Churchill quoting Clough's last verse (broadcast 27 April 1941) and choosing 'O God, our help' for the Prince of Wales service (10 August 1941); Bach's BWV 80 and five settings of Gerhardt's chorale in the St Matthew Passion; Bach at the Eisenach Latin school; Bonhoeffer's love of Psalm 119 (unfinished meditation, 1939-40); Mandela's signed passage in the 'Robben Island Bible' (16 December 1977). Texts typed from known public-domain versions: Clough, Watts, Hedge's 'A mighty fortress': PLEASE CHECK verbatim. Julius Caesar checked against Gutenberg #1522.
